about: Hand mapping from a fix to the kind of place it goes and SF's count of those places, read by ../fix-map.py. The lane files stay the source of every effect and cost; this file only says where each fix acts. place is a class or an expression over the classes in ../fix-reach.py ('&' and, '|' or, '!' not); a fix listed here takes the share of each mode x family group that sits in that place (within the entry's movement, if it names one) from out/crash-augment/profiles/fix-reach.json, in place of the lane's target_share text. units names a count in fix-reach.json's units, times units_scale; the per-unit cost is multiplied by it. life_years is used only where the lane record has none. text 'multiply' (per group in by_group) keeps the lane's own share where it names a party or crash type rather than a place (driver at fault, sideswipes), and multiplies it by the place's fraction of the group. After editing this file, run fix-reach.py, then fix-map.py.

life_source.title: Caltrans, Local Roadway Safety Manual, Version 1.8 (2026-05-11), Tables 1 to 3, Expected Life (years)

leading-pedestrian-interval.life_basis: LRSM SI22PB, Leading Pedestrian Interval, 10 years
leading-pedestrian-interval.why: an LPI is a signal phase, so it reaches only crashes at signals

citywide-signal-retiming-safe-speed.why: signal progression sets speeds at signals and along the arterial blocks between them

countdown-signals.scale_basis: eight modules at a typical four-leg intersection (the record's cost text)
countdown-signals.life_basis: LRSM SI18PB, pedestrian countdown signal heads, 20 years

dilemma-zone-detection.why: detection on high-speed approaches, which in SF are arterials

protected-left-turn-phase.why: a left-turn phase at signals on arterials, where permissive lefts cross several lanes

no-turn-on-red.scale_basis: one sign per approach at a four-leg intersection [inference — mine]
no-turn-on-red.life_basis: LRSM NS08, larger or additional stop or regulatory signs, 10 years (nearest sign item)
no-turn-on-red.why: turns on red happen only at signals

setback-stop-line-and-bike-box.life_basis: LRSM SI21PB, advance stop bar (bicycle box), 10 years

split-phase-bike-signal.life_basis: LRSM SI06, protected left turn phase, 20 years (nearest signal-phase item)
split-phase-bike-signal.why: a bike signal phase at signals on stressful streets

truncated-cycle-track.scale_basis: a curb extension on each approach [inference — mine]
truncated-cycle-track.life_basis: LRSM R34PB, separated bike lanes, 20 years
truncated-cycle-track.why: the corner end of a protected lane

all-way-stop-conversion.why: converts corners stopped on some approaches only

new-traffic-signal.why: a signal goes where an arterial crosses with no signal

roundabout-conversion.why: a full roundabout needs an arterial-size corner; the record's cost is the LADOT High band

mini-roundabout-traffic-circle.why: a traffic circle replaces stop control

raised-crosswalk-or-intersection.scale_basis: two raised crossings per intersection [inference — mine]
raised-crosswalk-or-intersection.why: raised crossings go at corners with no signal

raised-side-street-crossing.scale_basis: the two side-street mouths of an arterial crossing [inference — mine]
raised-side-street-crossing.life_basis: LRSM R37PB, raised pedestrian crossing, 20 years
raised-side-street-crossing.why: a raised crossing of the side street where it meets an arterial with no signal

high-visibility-crosswalk.scale_basis: two marked crossings per intersection [inference — mine]
high-visibility-crosswalk.life_basis: LRSM NS22PB, crossing at uncontrolled locations, signs and markings only, 10 years
high-visibility-crosswalk.why: the CMF is for marked crossings without a signal

pedestrian-hybrid-beacon.life_basis: LRSM NS25PB, pedestrian signal including PHB, 20 years
pedestrian-hybrid-beacon.why: a PHB stops arterial traffic at a crossing with no signal

median-refuge-island.life_basis: LRSM NS21PB, raised medians or refuge islands, 20 years
median-refuge-island.why: a refuge splits a long arterial crossing with no signal

curbed-median.why: medians run along multi-lane arterials; the record prices them per intersection island

left-turn-calming-hardened-centerline.why: left-turn calming where the turn crosses an arterial

curb-extension-tighter-corner.why: a corner program on the High Injury Network

daylighting-hardened.why: hardened daylighting on the High Injury Network

citywide-daylighting-every-corner.why: daylighting acts at corners; units stay SFMTA's 8,900 intersections from the record

parking-removal-near-junctions-and-on-bi.life_basis: the 10-year life in the record's own cost text
parking-removal-near-junctions-and-on-bi.why: red curb at corners with no signal, the place the record's shares name

lane-reduction-road-diet.why: a road diet takes a lane off a multi-lane arterial or collector

lane-narrowing-same-lanes.life_basis: LRSM R28, edge-lines and centerlines, 10 years (restriping)

corridor-traffic-calming-through-roads.life_basis: LRSM R28, edge-lines and centerlines, 10 years (the record prices paint and posts)
corridor-traffic-calming-through-roads.why: SF's quick-build corridors go on the High Injury Network

quick-build-separated-lane.life_basis: LRSM R34PB, separated bike lanes, 20 years
quick-build-separated-lane.why: protected lanes go on arterials and collectors

curb-protected-bike-lane.life_basis: LRSM R34PB, separated bike lanes, 20 years
curb-protected-bike-lane.why: protected lanes go on arterials and collectors

section-control-corridor-cameras.life_basis: LRSM R32, speed safety cameras, 10 years

citywide-default-20mph.why: the default covers SF's unposted 25 mph streets, which are residential and collector streets; the record's cost is one citywide sum

lower-speed-limits.scale_basis: the record prices a corridor of about 0.6 mile, so 1/0.6 corridors a mile
lower-speed-limits.why: AB 43 lets SF lower limits on safety corridors, which are its High Injury Network

area-wide-engineered-20mph-zones.why: humps and signs on residential streets; units stay the record's 887 unposted miles

vertical-calming-residential.scale_basis: about 14.2 devices a treated mile in SF (the record's unit text)
vertical-calming-residential.life_basis: the 15-year life the record for area-wide-engineered-20mph-zones gives the same SF devices

citywide-speed-camera-network.why: cameras sit on arterials and collectors (the record's own text); units stay the record's 320 to 740 locations

fixed-speed-cameras.why: today's 33 locations, within the street lane's corridor (the site's block and one more block each way); units stay the record's 33

slow-streets-network.scale_basis: the plan's 30 to 85 miles (record unit), about 57.5 at the middle, against the 575 street miles in candidate cells [inference — mine]
slow-streets-network.why: new Slow Streets go on low-stress residential streets inside cells; units stay the record's 30 to 85 miles

ltn-cell-program-citywide.why: cells and the crashes inside them counted by the same rule

not_placed.red-light-cameras: the record's cost field reads a $350,000 build cost per approach as a yearly cost, so a unit count would overstate the cost; needs the cost split before it is placed
not_placed.rotating-mobile-camera-coverage: the reach of a weekly-rotated unit is a share of time at each site, which no source gives
not_placed.midblock-pedestrian-signal: no count of midblock crossing sites
not_placed.speed-feedback-signs: no count of sign sites; the effect reaches a few hundred feet per sign
not_placed.street-lighting-upgrade: per-streetlight cost and no count of poorly lit blocks
not_placed.single-colored-bike-crossing: priced per square foot of marking, with no square footage per crossing
not_placed.superblock-and-car-free-centre-program: a superblock of about 9 blocks has no SF count
not_placed.school-streets-citywide-program: one-time set-up cost with no life, and the effect is for bell-time crashes, which needs an hour filter
not_placed.school-zone-measures: maps only to the cross-cut group of child pedestrians, which the stack does not count
not_placed.slip-lane-removal: no city dataset of slip lanes, and the record has no effect size
not_placed.grade-separated-crossing: per-bridge cost and no count of crossings that would need one
not_placed.crossing-guardrail: priced per linear foot of railing
not_placed.high-friction-surface: priced per square yard, and the wet-road share is not in the crash table
not_placed.systemic-hin-intersection-program: a bundle: its parts (LPI, daylighting, protected lefts) are placed and ranked on their own
not_placed.no-late-night-signal-flash: maps only to a cross-cut time group, which the stack does not count
